[new component]{.chip .built} [measurement]{.chip .measured} Entry 76 · milestone M4
:::

Each served output of the transport and EC surrogates now has an interval meant to contain
nine labels in ten, with a coverage measurement behind it. The method is split conformal
prediction. On a calibration split, the model's prediction errors are sorted. The interval
half-width is the error that nine in ten of those points stay within, with a small
correction for the finite sample. The intervals are then tested on held-out data that played
no part in training or calibration. The library is MAPIE. Every half-width is also checked
against the exact rank, and every stored record carries the hash of the model it belongs to.

The transport models were calibrated on their validation split. That split was sampled
uniformly over the kinetic input box, like most of the training data.

| test split | how it was drawn | coverage (6 outputs, 2 machines) |
|---|---|---|
| v1 test, v2-random | like the calibration data | 0.887–0.907 |
| v2 active-learning holdout | chosen by an earlier ensemble's disagreement | 0.909–0.955 |
| v3 test | states on held-out TORAX trajectories | 0.996–1.000 |

On the data drawn like the calibration split, coverage is close to nine in ten. For 10 000
calibration and 10 000 test points, exchangeable data would land between 0.893 and 0.907
nine times in ten. Nine of the twelve values fall in that range, and the other three miss
it by at most 0.006 ([90% intervals calibrated on the v1 validation split cover 0.887–0.907 on the v1 test and v2-random splits (6 outputs, ITER and MAST-U); 9 of 12 lie in the 0.893–0.907 range expected for exchangeable data, the other three miss it by at most 0.006]{.claim}[C-256](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-256){.cid .st-measured}). On the trajectory states the coupled runs
actually visit, the intervals over-cover ([the same intervals cover 0.996–1.000 of the v3 test states; there the half-width that would give 90% is 3.3–5.5 times smaller in signed-log units (ITER Q_e 0.48 against 2.21)]{.claim}[C-257](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-257){.cid .st-measured}). There, the error that nine in
ten points stay within is 3.3–5.5 times smaller in the model's signed-log units than across
the whole box. The intervals are wide for those states: for ITER's electron
heat flux, the interval spans a factor of about 9 on 1 + |Q|.

The EC surrogate was calibrated on 190 states from its four validation runs. These are the
states its guard accepts; the guard sends the others to the Gaussian fallback. On 548
served states from eight further runs, pooled coverage ranges from 0.876 for the heating
centre to 0.978 for absorbed power. All six outputs lie within or above the range expected
by chance ([90% intervals calibrated on 190 guard-accepted validation states (4 runs) cover 0.876–0.978 of 548 served test states (8 runs); all six outputs lie within or above the 0.856–0.938 range expected for exchangeable data; per-run coverage 0.78–1.00]{.claim}[C-258](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-258){.cid .st-measured}). States in one run are correlated, so coverage per run
varies more, from 0.78 to 1.00.

The pedestal model has no labelled data in this project, so it has no interval. Its record
says why.

None of this changes a deployed model, guard or tolerance. The intervals are evidence for
the M4 certification review, and later the surrogate-error terms for M5's uncertainty
propagation.

## What's next

We are awaiting a decision on adding a calibration on trajectory states for M5. The
remaining M4 steps are output bounds, local robustness, the EC closed loop and guard
integration, followed by the certification review.
